cards.text: It's the fourth year of King Darius of Persia (Ezra 4:24), and on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev, the word of the LORD comes to the prophet Zechariah. Now the people of Bethel have sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, along with their men, to plead before the LORD. And friend, they did not come for small talk.

cards.question: The men sent from Bethel want to plead before the LORD. So who do they bring their question to?

answers.text: The elders of their own town

cards.text: Here's their question: "Should I weep and fast in the fifth month, as I have done these many years?" That's the meeting that's been on your calendar for YEARS, and one brave soul finally asks, "Wait. Are we still doing this?"
Then the word of the LORD of Hosts comes to Zechariah. And this time, the LORD has some questions of His own.

cards.question: The LORD tells Zechariah to ask all the people of the land and the priests.
The people have fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months for seventy years. What does God ask them about it?

answers.text: Whether it was really for Him

cards.text: Then God asks about their eating and drinking: weren't they doing that simply for themselves? That's me telling the bakers I'm taste-testing the batch for THEM. Six cookies in.
Then God asks one more question: aren't these the words He already proclaimed in earlier days?

cards.question: God asks if these are the words He proclaimed in earlier days. Who did He proclaim them through?
Back when the earlier prophets spoke, Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were empty.

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Zechariah again, with a message from the LORD of Hosts. Listen close, because this one's all about how people treat each other.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts tells them to administer true justice.

cards.text: The LORD of Hosts also says to show loving devotion and compassion to one another. Real simple, real hard.

cards.question: God names the widow, the fatherless, the foreigner and the poor, and says do not ___ them.

cards.text: And one more: do not plot evil in your hearts against one another. Now the passage turns to how the people answered all this.

cards.question: When God gave them these commands, the people paid close attention.

cards.text: They refused, turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped up their ears. That's all of us with the snooze button: the alarm is RIGHT THERE going off, and we just roll over and pull the pillow over our ears.

cards.question: God says the people made their hearts like flint. What's that picture saying?

answers.text: Their hearts were hard and unbending
Their hearts were soft and easy to shape
Their hearts were warm and wide open

cards.text: They would not listen to the law or to the words the LORD of Hosts had sent by His Spirit through the earlier prophets. Therefore great anger came from the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says He called and the people would not listen. So what happens when they call to Him?

answers.text: He would send a new prophet

cards.question: The LORD says He scattered the people with a whirlwind. Where did they end up?

answers.text: Among nations they had not known
Out in the wilderness of Sinai

cards.question: Once the people were scattered, the land behind them was left ___ so that no one could come or go.

cards.text: They turned the pleasant land into a desolation. Hold that thought, friend, because Bethel's question about fasting is still sitting on the table.
